name: session.bootstrap
description: Set up a new connection in one call: receive events, list sessions, and attach.

attach_session_ids.description: The sessions to attach to, in order. Unknown and repeated IDs are skipped, and an empty list attaches none. Leave it out to let the server pick one.

creator_name.description: Issue tickets for blocks whose creator_name is this, such as com.superlogical.terminal. Required.

data_ref_id.description: Which of each block's data sources the ticket opens, such as terminal.

subprotocol.description: The subprotocol the data connection will use, such as rex.data.terminal.v1. If set, each ticket works only on a connection that uses it.

data_tickets.description: The kinds of block to issue data tickets for. The response has a ticket for each visible block in an attached session that matches one. At most 8 entries.

event_scope.description: Which events to receive. 'session' sends every session's events except block_event, plus session_created, session_destroyed, session_moved, and tailscale_status_changed. 'all' also sends block_event and the client events, such as client_joined.

preferred_session_id.description: The session to attach to, if it exists. Otherwise the server attaches the first session it can. Ignored when attach_session_ids is set.

sessions.description: Every session on the server when this connection started receiving events.

attach_all.description: What session.attach_all returns: every session on the server when this connection started receiving events.

active_window_id.description: The window the session shows. Left out when the session has no windows.

revision.description: The view's revision. A larger revision is a newer view of the session, even across a server restart. It goes up by one with each change, and jumps ahead when a restarted server restores the session.

focused_block_id.description: The window's focused block, which receives typing while the window is active. Left out if the window has none.

creator_name.description: The creator that made the block, such as com.superlogical.terminal.

flavor.description: The flavor the block was made from, such as com.superlogical.terminal.shell.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the block runs as. If it equals your local server's host_id, the block sees the same files you do. Otherwise treat the block as remote.

owner.description: The client that owns the block. Left out when the block has no owner.

blocks.description: The blocks in the layer, in layout order. The layout field says where each one sits.

bounds.description: Where the layer sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

kind.description: How the layer is placed: 'tiled' for the layer that fills the window, or 'floating' for a floating layer. Draw a kind you don't know as 'floating'.

block_id.description: The block at this node. Set only when split isn't.

rect.description: Where this node sits, as [x, y, w, h] fractions of the window's width and height.

after.description: The node on the right or bottom.

before.description: The node on the left or top.

direction.description: How the space is divided: 'horizontal' puts before on the left and after on the right, and 'vertical' puts before above after. Draw a direction you don't know as 'horizontal'.

ratio.description: The fraction of the space that before gets, between 0 and 1.

split_id.description: The split's ID. It stays the same while the split exists, so you can match splits across views.

split.description: How this node divides in two. Set only when block_id isn't.

layout.description: How the layer divides its space between blocks, as a tree of splits. Null when the layer is empty.

state.description: How the layer is presented: 'minimized' means don't draw it, though its blocks keep running, and only a floating layer can be minimized. Left out for a normal layer. Draw a state you don't know as normal.

layers.description: The window's layers, from back to front. The first is the tiled layer, which holds the window's layout and fills the window.

zoomed_block_id.description: The block zoomed to fill the window, if any. Layouts keep their normal sizes, so draw this block over the whole window.

windows.description: The session's windows, in order. Rex.app shows them as tabs in this order.

view.description: The session's view, read after the connection started receiving its events. Apply it first, then the events whose seq is higher than the response's.

attached_sessions.description: The sessions attached from attach_session_ids, in the order requested. Sessions that don't exist are left out, and so may be sessions that are being destroyed.

client_id.description: This connection's client ID, the same one session.attach returns. Present even when no session is attached.

data_ref_id.description: The data source the ticket opens.

expires_in_ms.description: How long the ticket stays valid after the server issues it, in milliseconds.

session_id.description: The session that holds the block.

subprotocol.description: The subprotocol the ticket is bound to. Left out if the request named none.

ticket.description: A single-use ticket to send in the HELLO message that opens the data connection. Only a data connection from the same user can use it.

data_tickets.description: A data ticket for each visible block in the returned views that matches an entry of the request's data_tickets. Call data.connect for a block that has none.

active_window_id.description: The window the session shows. Left out when the session has no windows.

revision.description: The view's revision. A larger revision is a newer view of the session, even across a server restart. It goes up by one with each change, and jumps ahead when a restarted server restores the session.

split_id.description: The split's ID. It stays the same while the split exists, so you can match splits across views.

split.description: How this node divides in two. Set only when block_id isn't.

layout.description: How the layer divides its space between blocks, as a tree of splits. Null when the layer is empty.

zoomed_block_id.description: The block zoomed to fill the window, if any. Layouts keep their normal sizes, so draw this block over the whole window.

windows.description: The session's windows, in order. Rex.app shows them as tabs in this order.

view.description: The session's view, read after the connection started receiving its events. Apply it first, then the events whose seq is higher than the response's.

selected_session.description: The session the server chose and attached. Null if you sent attach_session_ids, or if no session could be attached.

api_min_revision.description: The oldest revision of the API the server supports. Left out when it is 0.

api_revision.description: The newest revision of the API the server supports. Left out when it is 0.

generation.description: How many times the server has loaded its configuration file since it started, counting from 1. It goes up on every load, even one that fails.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the configuration file and the modules it requires while it loads, in lowercase hexadecimal. Empty if there's no file or it couldn't be read.

config.description: The configuration file the server loaded most recently. Always present, even when there is no file.

exit_empty.description: True if the server stops on its own soon after its last session and last connection close.

host_id.description: Identifies the machine and account the server runs as. Servers that see the same files report the same value. Left out when the server has no state directory.

instance_id.description: A random ID for this run of the server. A new value means a new server process, even if pid is the same.

addresses.description: The addresses the listener is bound to, such as a socket path or 127.0.0.1:54321. They show the port that an endpoint like 127.0.0.1:0 got. Left out when the server can't tell.

admission.description: Which callers the listener lets in: 'peer_credentials', 'anonymous', 'tailscale_owner', 'tailscale_identified', or 'login_server'. Left out when the server can't tell. Show a value you don't know as it is.

endpoint.description: The endpoint the listener was configured with, such as unix:///run/rex.sock, 127.0.0.1:7297, or tailnet://:7297.

primary.description: True for the server's primary endpoint, where commands such as rex server status and rex server stop look for the server. Left out for the other listeners.

transport.description: How the listener identifies its callers: 'unix', 'named_pipe', 'tcp', or 'tailscale'. Show a value you don't know as it is.

listeners.description: Each endpoint the server accepts connections on, primary first. Servers older than API revision 12 leave it out. Doesn't include built-in Tailscale, which the tailscale member describes.

session_count.description: How many sessions the server has.

started_at.description: When the server started, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

login_name.description: The Tailscale login name, usually an email address. For display only, because it can change.

account.description: The Tailscale account that signed the device in. Left out until Tailscale reports it.

allow_tailnet_members.description: True if anyone your tailnet's access rules allow may connect. False lets in only the Tailscale user who signed the device in.

auth_url.description: The link to open to sign the device in to Tailscale. Present while state is needs_login, once Tailscale has made the link.

control_url.description: The control server the device uses, such as a Headscale server. Left out for Tailscale's own, while built-in Tailscale is off, and by older servers.

dns_name.description: The device's MagicDNS name, such as rex.tail1234.ts.net. Left out until known.

error.description: Why built-in Tailscale turned off after its HTTPS listener failed. The next enable clears it.

state.description: 'pending' until the HTTPS listener is ready, then 'available'. The server is reachable over the tailnet only when available. Treat a value you don't know as 'pending'.

url.description: The server's address on the tailnet, such as https://rex.tail1234.ts.net. Present once HTTPS is available and the device's name is known.

https.description: The state of the device's HTTPS listener. Left out while built-in Tailscale is off, and by older servers.

state.description: 'disabled' (off), 'starting', 'needs_login' (see auth_url), 'needs_machine_approval' (a tailnet admin must approve the device), or 'running' (on the tailnet). Treat a value you don't know as 'starting'.

tags.description: The Tailscale tags the device has, such as tag:rex. A tagged device has no owner. Left out when it has none.

tailnet_name.description: The tailnet's display name, or its domain if it has none. Left out until known.

tailscale.description: The status of built-in Tailscale. Present only when the server can run it.

server_status.description: The server's status, as server.status returns it.

validation_notes: Send it as the first request on a new connection. Apply its result first, then each event whose `seq` is higher than the response's `seq`, even one that arrived before the response.
`event_scope` works as it does for `session.attach_all`, and the connection can then call methods on any session. A value other than `session` or `all` fails with `bad_request`.
If `attach_session_ids` is left out, the server attaches one session and returns it in `selected_session`, which is null when the server has no sessions.
If `attach_session_ids` is set, even to an empty array, the server returns the sessions it attached in `attached_sessions` and leaves `selected_session` null.

A session in `attach_session_ids` that is destroyed during the call is left out of `attached_sessions`. If the session chosen for `selected_session` is destroyed during the call, the call fails with `session_not_found`. Any other failure to attach also fails the whole call.
If the connection falls more than 8 MiB of events behind, the server closes it rather than skip events. Open a new connection and call `session.bootstrap` again.
If the call fails, close the connection and open a new one before you try again. Part of the setup may already have taken effect.
